column2: Docs current and consistent with the code [SO2]
column6: The five documents this criterion covers (docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and the AI context file, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) exist, are in the PDF, rendered and matching the named commit, and pass the spot-check: docs/design.md describes the system that exists, and docs/requirements.md gives an acceptance criterion wherever a requirement's behavior is not obvious (for a finished functional requirement, the name of its test in CI will do), and lists under Constraints the limits the team did not choose. Whether the README.md quickstart runs is scored under Build health. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: One of the five is absent from the repository or has drifted from the code, one is missing from the PDF, not rendered, or does not match the named commit, or some are missing sections. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column12: Two or more of the five are absent from the repository or have drifted from the code, or two or more are missing from the PDF, not rendered, or do not match the named commit. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.

column6: docs/risks.md is the single risk register, changed since the last checkpoint, ranked, and with owners; it is in the PDF, rendered and matching the named commit, and no duplicate register exists elsewhere. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: Risks are tracked but incompletely: ranking or owners missing on some risks, the register has not changed since the last checkpoint, a second register exists, or docs/risks.md is missing from the PDF, not rendered, or does not match the named commit. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column12: No docs/risks.md or an empty one, or a register with neither ranking nor owners. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.

column6: CI passed on the named commit and runs the tests on every pull request (if you contribute to an open-source project, that project's CI on your pull requests, or the build-and-test command your fork documents until your first one); at least one test would fail if the feature it covers broke; a grader can follow the quickstart from a clean checkout without help. The checks match how much the team delegates: review gates on the changes that are expensive to undo (schema, authentication, deployment, migrations), changes exercised somewhere other than production before they reach users (a staging or preview environment, a store beta track, a dedicated test device, a run on sample data), and a documented rollback path.
column9: CI and tests exist, but the quickstart runs only with a step README.md does not give, or the checks have visible gaps relative to how the team works: no gate on a hard-to-undo path, nowhere to exercise changes before they reach users, or no documented rollback path.
column12: CI is absent or red, no test would fail if the feature it covers broke, the quickstart does not work, or changes reach production with no gate and no rollback path.

column2: Contribution traceability and version control hygiene [SO5]
column6: Each student's work is attributable over the period: code through reviewed PRs under real accounts, other work where CONTRIBUTING.md says it lives, and the Contribution lines in the sprint notes match that record. The history is one a maintainer could inherit: nothing lands on the default branch outside a pull request; no live secrets, build artifacts, or dependency directories are in the history (if a secret leaked, it was revoked or rotated, and the commit that removed it says so); commit messages say what changed and why, with noisy branches squashed on merge; nobody force-pushes the default branch; and large binaries are out of Git or in Git LFS.
column9: Most students' work is traceable, but some of it cannot be attributed, or the history misses any of those items (direct commits to the default branch, committed build artifacts or dependency directories, commit messages that do not say what changed and why, noisy branches merged unsquashed, a force-push to the default branch, large binaries outside Git LFS).
column12: Contribution cannot be traced to individuals over the period, or a secret was committed and never rotated.

column6: Every milestone item for this checkpoint is met, with its evidence: the release candidate built from the named commit (linked on the cover) and the real-user session (notes in the PDF). Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: One milestone item is unmet or only demonstrable with help, and the cover names it with an owner and a date to close it (e.g., the install needs a step README.md does not give, or the session notes leave out what the participant tried or the change a finding produced).
column12: Two or more milestone items are unmet, or one is unmet and the cover names no owner and date to close it.
